Anika (Eng): Heads-up: I'm planning to move to Sydney for ~120 days starting 2027-11-10 to help with family logistics and remote work. Can we confirm WFH stipend, whether this triggers local payroll registration, superannuation, and any visa/employment changes?
Jared (People Ops): Thanks for flagging, Anika. 120 days is >90 so this could change things. Quick Q: are you staying on your current employment contract and pay currency? Any client/customer meetings planned?
Anika (Eng): Same contract, USD payroll. No local contracting or consulting. Might attend a customer meetup but nothing billed locally.
Priya (Payroll): Important: >90 days may create employer obligations in Australia. We need to know if you'll be physically present in the same state/office as other Redwoods. Also we may need to route pay through our AUS payroll partner or add local payroll reporting.
Sonia (Tax): Correct — Australia has employer obligations like PAYG withholding and potentially superannuation contributions for employees working in Australia even temporarily, depending on visa/status and whether the employer has a 'permanent place of business' there. 120 days is significant; we'll assess but expect at least documentation and possibly withholding.
Nico (Legal): Also check visa status. If you're on a tourist visa, local employment rules still apply. If you switch to a local visa with work permission, that could require local employment registration. Don't accept local offers or sign anything labeled "engagement" without legal review.
Anika (Eng): I'm on a tourist visa. No offers expected. Main asks: (1) Will I keep Redwood travel insurance? (2) If we need to route pay locally how quickly can that happen?
Jared (People Ops): (1) Travel insurance remains primary for medical/emergency while on a tourist visa; we can advise on local options if needed. (2) Payroll routing can take 4-6 weeks if local vendor setup required. We should aim to decide ASAP to avoid payroll disruption.
Priya (Payroll): Action: please fill the /forms/temp-remote with exact dates, address, and emergency contact. Also upload passport page and visa stamp. We'll run a payroll impact check.
peopleops-bot: Reminder: Complete /forms/temp-remote within 48h to avoid payroll delays.
Sonia (Tax): We'll start a quick risk assessment: 1) confirm days present, 2) whether you meet any Australian tax residency tests, 3) whether employer has permanent place of business (we don't currently), 4) whether superannuation applies. Typically for short-term employees on foreign payroll super contributions may still be due if the work is performed in Australia and the arrangement looks like local employment.
Nico (Legal): We'll also confirm whether any contract amendments are needed (e.g., add clause for temporary local compliance). Don't sign any local vendor or accommodation contracts that imply local business operations on Redwood's behalf.
Anika (Eng): Noted. If superannuation applies, how is that calculated and who pays?
Sonia (Tax): Superannuation (SG) is typically ~11% of ordinary time earnings; if it applies to a foreign employer we may need to remit on top of salary. There are exemptions for short-term/temporary postings under certain double-tax or social security agreements, but Australia doesn't have a wide-ranging social security totalization with the US. We'll check bilateral rules and escalate to payroll ops.
Priya (Payroll): If super is required, payroll will add separate employer-side contributions to be remitted to an Australian fund. That would be an additional cost to Redwood; we'll need approval from finance for any extra spend.
Jared (People Ops): Practical proposal: start with provisional approval for up to 30 days remote in Australia while tax/legal complete full assessment. If risk requires local payroll/super, we'll propose either (A) convert to local payroll for duration or (B) reduce stay to <90 days. Which do you prefer, Anika?
Anika (Eng): Prefer to keep the full 120 days if possible. If conversion to local payroll is required I need clarity on net pay impact (currency conversion, tax withholding).
Nico (Legal): We'll draft an FAQ for you covering: visa/do's & don'ts, contracting constraints, travel insurance scope, data residency considerations (if you handle customer data locally), and approvals needed for in-person customer events.
peopleops-bot: Temp Remote Request logged (ID #TR-2027-910).
Sonia (Tax): Next steps: Anika submits forms & docs; Tax will prepare preliminary memo within 3 business days outlining likely obligations and scenarios (no-super, super-required, full payroll registration).
Priya (Payroll): Parallel: I'll run a payroll-run impact simulation (net pay delta if AUS withholding applies) and estimate vendor setup lead time. Expect initial results in 5 business days.
Jared (People Ops): I'll mark thread status "pending tax/payroll assessment" and propose provisional 30-day approval to avoid forcing an immediate return. If tax says conversion required, we'll discuss options.
Anika (Eng): Thanks — submitted the form and attached passport + flight itinerary. Appreciate the quick triage.
Sonia (Tax): Received. We'll email a short memo and loop finance if employer-side contributions are required.
Priya (Payroll): Logged: payroll simulation queued (ID #PR-2027-AUS-01). Will post numbers here when ready.
Nico (Legal): Drafting temporary remote checklist addendum to cover >90-day cases; will share for comments.
Jared (People Ops): Thanks team. Closing when tax + payroll post their memos. Anika: if anything changes to dates please update the form.
Anika (Eng): Will do. Thanks all for the fast responses. :thumbsup:
